title: Aston Villa analysis: Depleted in defeat but not down
description: Pre-game, captain John McGinn promised Aston Villa fans they could still expect "as much as possible" this season despite the high-profile exits of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans.  A battling performance in Austria backed those words up as, even in this defeat by PSG, Villa scared the European champions for a second time in 18 months, following their 5-4 Champions League last-eight defeat in 2025.  No Ollie Watkins, Emi Martinez and Ezri Konsa - given more time off after the World Cup - which allowed teenager Brian Madjo to finally show what he can do after Villa won their appeal to register him, and 19-year-old midfielder George Hemmings also getting a start.
fullText:
Pre-game, captain John McGinn promised Aston Villa fans they could still expect "as much as possible" this season despite the high-profile exits of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans.

A battling performance in Austria backed those words up as, even in this defeat by PSG, Villa scared the European champions for a second time in 18 months, following their 5-4 Champions League last-eight defeat in 2025.

No Ollie Watkins, Emi Martinez and Ezri Konsa - given more time off after the World Cup - which allowed teenager Brian Madjo to finally show what he can do after Villa won their appeal to register him, and 19-year-old midfielder George Hemmings also getting a start.

The positives were also evident despite the loss, with Boubacar Kamara also playing his first competitive match since a serious knee injury in January.

Villa should be stronger for the Premier League season opener at Brighton on 23 August, with the club due to be active in the final two weeks of the transfer window.

Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri is poised to join this week, while they have not given up on their chase for Bayern Munich midfielder Joao Palhinha.

Ever the perfectionist, boss Emery will be frustrated by the loss - especially as it was his fourth defeat in the competition - but as Villa enter a new era there is a lot of cause for optimism.

title: Hamilton West Side tops Kentucky, reaches Little League World Series
description: The Hamilton West Side Little League baseball team has reached the Little League World Series for the first time since 2021.
fullText:
The Hamilton West Side Little League baseball team has reached the Little League World Series for the first time since 2021 after defeating Kentucky's North Oldham, 6-0, in Whitestown, Indiana, in the Great Lakes region championship game on ESPN2.

The 2026 Little League World Series begins on Wednesday, Aug. 19, in Williamsport, Pennsylvania. As the Great Lakes region winner, West Side will face the yet-to-be-determined Mountain Region champion on Aug. 20 at 2 p.m.

West Side starter Boone Treadway, the son of Badin head coach Brion Treadway, pitched a one-hit, complete-game shutout. He threw 62 pitches, and struck out nine.

"Feels amazing," Treadway told ESPN after the game. "I'm just glad to get to do it with this group of kids."

Josiah Infante hit a two-run homer during West Side's six-run first inning.

West Side is a 23-time Ohio state champion. In 2021, West Side advanced to the LLWS final before losing to Michigan.

West Side and North Oldham met twice in the Great Lakes regional. West Side won the first meeting, 11-4.

West Side cruised past Michigan and Indiana in the first two rounds of the tournament.

title: Sara Curtis of Italy breaks world record in 50m backstroke
description: Sara Curtis took two tenths off Australian Kaylee McKeown's world record.
fullText:
Italian Sara Curtis broke the world record in the 50m backstroke at the European Swimming Championships in Paris.

Curtis, a University of Virginia rising sophomore, clocked 26.63 seconds in Wednesday's semifinals, taking 23 hundredths off Australian Kaylee McKeown's world record of 26.86 set in 2023.

The 50m backstroke makes its Olympic debut in 2028, along with the 50m breaststroke and 50m butterfly. The 50m freestyle has been on the Olympic program since 1988.

Curtis made her Olympic debut in 2024, reaching the semifinals of the 50m free and placing eighth with the Italian women's 4x100m free relay.

Curtis' previous personal best was 27.07 seconds, ranking her fifth on the all-time performer list before today's world record.

Also at Europeans, Olympic champion Hubert Kos of Hungary swam the second-fastest men's 200m backstroke in history in Tuesday's semifinals — a 1:52.30, second only to American Aaron Peirsol's world record of 1:51.92 from 2009. The men's 200m back is one of just three individual world records still standing from the super-suit era of 2008-09.

Romanian David Popovici swam the third-fastest men's 100m free in history — a 46.56, just off China's Pan Zhanle's world record of 46.40 from the 2024 Olympics. Popovici also has the second-fastest time in history, a 46.51 from winning the 2025 World title.

Swede Sarah Sjostrom won the women's 50m butterfly at Europeans, her 97th career medal among the Olympics, World Championships (long course and short course) and Europeans (long course and short course) and her first since becoming a mom last August.

title: Lampard believes Haji Wright ready for Premier League
description: After struggling to find the field during the World Cup, Wright is ready to lead Coventry into the Premiership.
fullText:
The 2026-27 Premier League season begins next week, and 20 teams enter with dreams renewed for the new year. For Coventry City, who earned promotion to the Premier League after winning the EFL Championship, it will be a chance to compete in the top flight for the first time since the 2000-01 season. And USMNT forward Haji Wright will be a big part of their offense this season.

Wright was one of the major factors behind Coventry's promotion last season, with 18 goals and 2 assists in 40 appearances for the Sky Blues across all competitions. However, he struggled to find any playing time for the USMNT during the 2026 World Cup, with just two minute-long appearances logged for the tournament.

Still, Coventry has relied on him to score goals, and he's done that since he arrived there in August 2023. In 124 total appearances, he's scored 49 goals and added 11 assists. It's that kind of production that head coach Frank Lampard feels has prepared Haji Wright for the rigors of the Premier League.

"When you come into a job, you evaluate the talent in the squad and the need for goals at the top end of the pitch. Haji already had a record as such," Lampard said, speaking exclusively to Stars & Stripes FC. "He was playing on the left wing sometimes under the previous manager, but I felt quite quickly that he's a No. 9 and he prefers to be in that position too. I think it makes the most of his talents and attributes, with his speed, size and ability to run in behind defenses. It will be a big test for him, as with all the players, because there's a big gap with the Premier League. They must be focused on bridging that gap with belief. I think Haji absolutely has the talent to succeed here in the Premier League."

For Lampard, the hope is that Wright is able to continue his goal production to help keep Coventry in the top flight. Most teams that are promoted to the Premier League struggle in that first season, with a big percentage of them getting relegated back to the Championship after one year. Coventry hope to dodge the relegation slide and do what they can to stay afloat. And for Wright, it's a chance to show that he is a dependable striker in one of the best leagues in the world and that he can produce against some of the best defenses on the planet.

Coventry have a tall task ahead of them, as they open up the season on the road on August 21st to defending Premier League champions Arsenal. Three of their first four matches will come against teams that finished in the top 8 in last season's table: Arsenal, Manchester City, and Brighton & Hove Albion. It will truly be a big test for Haji Wright and the Sky Blues as they prepare for their first Premier League season in 25 years.

title: History Says Red Sox Have 50% Chance to Win World Series for This Reason
description: This would be a perfect outcome for the Red Sox.
fullText:
History Says Red Sox Have 50% Chance to Win World Series for This Reason originally appeared on NESN. 

Going 27-3 at any stretch in a season in Major League Baseball is flat-out ridiculous. There's a reason why what the Boston Red Sox did was historic, though it doesn't necessarily guarantee that they're going to win a World Series.

We've seen this happen six other times in Major League Baseball history, and the Red Sox are the only team that has ever been more than four games under at their lowest point. ESPN recently did a breakdown of the six teams that have gone 27-3 during the season over the past 100 years, and the Red Sox are the weirdest team of the bunch.

Boston was 37-48 before their streak and was 14 games under .500 at one point. Every other team was above .500 by multiple games before their stretch. What makes matters even more interesting is that three of the six won a World Series.

"1936 Giants 49-44 Lost World Series 1941 Yankees 33-24 Won World Series 1947 Yankees 27-23 Won World Series 1953 Yankees 17-9 Won World Series 1977 Royals 64-51 Lost ALCS 2017 Indians 69-56 Lost ALDS," ESPN posted.

A 50% chance for the Red Sox here, history-wise, is pretty much as good a chance as any other team in Major League Baseball has ever had.

Obviously, there's no guarantee that Boston will even come close to winning the World Series, as this season has been very strange. However, history says that a 50% chance is in the works.

It's probably only fair to say that if Red Sox fans were told they had a 50% chance to win a World Series based on a couple of stats at the beginning of the season.

title: Dubois unification moves closer as Turhan joins MVP
description: Turkish lightweight world champion Elif Nur Turhan signs with Most Valuable Promotions, bringing a potential unification fight with Briton Caroline Dubois a step closer.
fullText:
Turkish lightweight world champion Elif Nur Turhan has signed with Most Valuable Promotions, bringing a potential unification fight with Briton Caroline Dubois a step closer.

Turhan was previously signed to Matchroom Boxing but joins MVP as part of a new strategic alliance between the two promotions.

The 31-year-old has won all 14 of her professional bouts, with eight victories by stoppage, and holds the IBF lightweight title.

"Forces have been joined. As female boxers, we will now move forward with greater strength," Turhan said.

"I am excited for the opportunities that will come my way as I look to win more major world titles."

Londoner Dubois - also with MVP - will defend her WBC and WBO lightweight titles against American Amelia Moore on 29 August on an all-female card in Birmingham.

American Stephanie Han, the WBA lightweight champion, is also signed to MVP.

"The Golden Turkish Warrior [Turhan] is one of the most exciting fighters in boxing given her immense punching power and her relentless aggressive, pressure heavy style," MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian said.

"Signing Elif will allow us to make some of the most exciting fights in boxing."

Last month, MVP announced the new partnership with Matchroom, designed to create more opportunities for female fighters across both promotional rosters.

The agreement is expected to create more crossover opportunities, allowing fighters from both promotions to compete on each other's cards.

Turhan joins Australian two-weight world champion Skye Nicolson in making the move from Matchroom to MVP.

MVP also merged with the Professional Fighters League in July to bring together a roster of more than 300 fighters across boxing and mixed martial arts (MMA).

title: GB dressage team qualify for LA28 Olympics
description: The Great Britain dressage team secure qualification for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles by winning silver at the FEI World Championships in Aachen, Germany.
fullText:
The Great Britain dressage team secured qualification for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles by winning silver at the FEI World Championships in Aachen, Germany.

Fiona Bigwood, Charlotte Fry, Carl Hester and Becky Moody finished on a score of 231.4 in the dressage team final, with home nation Germany taking gold on 235.0.

Bigwood, aboard Donna Bella, and Moody, on Jagerbomb, had put GB into second spot on Tuesday.

Hester, on Fame, and defending individual and freestyle world champion Fry, who rode Glamourdale and top scored for the team with 80.311, went on Wednesday and secured second spot.

The top six teams from the event qualified for LA28; Denmark finished third, Belgium were fourth, the Netherlands in fifth and Sweden sixth.

title: O'Sullivan suffers another setback with China Open exit
description: Ronnie O'Sullivan suffers another defeat as his poor start to the season continued with a 6-4 loss to Noppon Saengkham in the second round of the China Open, with world champion Wu Yize also out.
fullText:
Ronnie O'Sullivan suffered another setback as his poor start to the season continued with a 6-4 loss to Noppon Saengkham in the second round of the China Open.

The 50-year-old, who has won the tournament twice, was 3-1 up before losing four straight frames.

The seven-time world champion responded before losing the final frame 64-46 to add to his second-round exit at the Shanghai Masters last month.

Thailand's Saengkham is ranked 45th in the world and has now beaten O'Sullivan in back-to-back matches.

Having started slowly in the first round, the Englishman won six straight frames to beat Wales' Jackson Page 6-2.

Saengkham, 34, will now face Shaun Murphy, who defeated China's Xiao Guodong 6-2.

World champion Wu Yize also crashed out following a 6-2 loss to England's David Gilbert.

title: Neto attracting Premier League interest
description: Chelsea winger Pedro Neto has attracted interest from four Premier League clubs, with one believed to be Manchester City.  The 26-year-old Portugal international is not regarded as one of the 'untouchable' players at Stamford Bridge and could therefore move before the transfer deadline.  The club believe the market for wide forwards has been inflated by a lack of options for leading clubs, highlighted by the £117m fee paid for Morgan Rogers and Paris St-Germain's £145m valuation of Bradley Barcola.
fullText:
Chelsea winger Pedro Neto has attracted interest from four Premier League clubs, with one believed to be Manchester City.

The 26-year-old Portugal international is not regarded as one of the 'untouchable' players at Stamford Bridge and could therefore move before the transfer deadline.

However, Chelsea insist they would demand a significant fee for the attacker, who joined from Wolves for £54m in 2024.

The club believe the market for wide forwards has been inflated by a lack of options for leading clubs, highlighted by the £117m fee paid for Morgan Rogers and Paris St-Germain's £145m valuation of Bradley Barcola.

Those figures have influenced Chelsea's valuation of Neto, who is known to be of interest to Manchester City where he would be reunited with former Blues boss Enzo Maresca.

Maresca and Neto are understood to have a strong relationship, and the winger is among those reported to have been frustrated by the Italian's departure midway through last season.

New manager Xabi Alonso has not commented on Neto's future, but he has played the winger in pre-season friendlies, including the 3-0 win over AC Milan on Saturday.

title: Bayonne now one win away from advancing to Little League World Series
description: Bayonne Little League is closing in on history, one win away from becoming the first Hudson County team to advance to the Little League World Series.
fullText:
Bayonne Little League is closing in on history.

With a win in Friday night's Metro Region championship game, the reigning New Jersey state champions would advance to the Little League World Series, becoming the first Hudson County team to accomplish the feat and first New Jersey charter since Toms River East did it in 2021.

Bayonne will face the winner of Game 5 between New York (PYA Port Washington) and Connecticut (Darien) in the Aug. 14 championship game. The New Jersey state champions have already secured a spot in the title matchup after opening the Metro Region tournament with convincing victories over Connecticut and New York.

Bayonne (13-0) won both its games this week in Bristol, Connecticut, outscoring its first two opponents, 20-4. The Bees have been dominant, opening with an 8-2 victory over Connecticut before overwhelming New York, 12-2, two days later.

In the win over New York, Mason Rincon set the tone early by blasting a two-run home run to center field. Later in the first inning, AJ Tapia lined a single down the right-field line to drive in two more runs, giving Bayonne a 4-0 lead after one inning.

Bayonne continued to pour on the offense, adding one run in the second inning, five 

Gabriel Garcia Jr. and Mason Rincon combined to pitch all four innings, with Garcia earning the victory. He worked the first two innings, allowing three hits and two earned runs while helping keep the Bees firmly in control. Rincon handled the final two innings as Bayonne closed out the 12-2 win under the run rule.

Since Bayonne has not played since Aug. 10, the team will have had several days to rest and prepare for the championship game.

Aston Villa are reportedly in talks to sign DR Congo international right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

fullText:
Jose Mourinho finally has his full Real Madrid squad back together after Jude Bellingham returned to training following his extended summer break.

The England international completed his commercial commitments in London before making his way back to the club, becoming the final World Cup international to report for duty.

As the clubBellingham took part in the afternoon session alongside the players who were not selected for Real Madrid's Teresa Herrera Trophy meeting with Deportivo La Coruna at Riazor.

His return will be welcomed by Mourinho, who has been gradually integrating the squad ahead of the new season.

The midfielder is also said to be in excellent physical condition, meaning there should be little concern over his fitness as he begins his preparations.

However, Bellingham will not feature against Deportivo.

Bellingham's arrival completes an important stage of Real Madrid's pre-season preparations.

The 23-year-old had been given additional time away following his international commitments, while several of his teammates had already returned to work earlier in the week.

Mourinho now has the majority of his senior group available, although the players who recently reported back are still being managed carefully.

Bellingham trained with and without the ball during the session, beginning the process of getting back up to full match sharpness.

The midfielder was joined by the injured members of the squad, although those players followed individual programmes.

Jude Bellingham is the last player to rejoin training after the World Cup. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

As such, the likes of Raul Asencio, Rodrygo, Eder Militao, Ferland Mendy and Thiago Pitarch were among those continuing their recovery work away from the main group.

Bellingham's first opportunity to play under Mourinho is now expected to come against Schalke on Sunday, August 16.

That gives him several days to work with the first-team group and become accustomed to Mourinho's methods before stepping onto the pitch.

Speaking of the Teresa Herrera Trophy, Kylian Mbappe, Marc Cucurella, Ibrahima Konate and Aurelien Tchouameni are all unavailable for the trip to Riazor despite having returned to training earlier this week.

Rather than immediately throwing the returning internationals into action, Mourinho is giving them time to build their fitness and adapt to the workload.

title: Torres misses Barcelona training to finalise PSG move
description: Spain's World Cup hero Ferran Torres is given permission to miss Barcelona training to finalise a move to Paris St-Germain.
fullText:
Spain's World Cup hero Ferran Torres has been given permission to miss Barcelona training to finalise a move to Paris St-Germain.

Torres, 26, scored an extra-time winner against Argentina to help Spain claim their second World Cup this summer.

He had been due to return to training with the Catalan giants on Wednesday but will not do so as a move to PSG gets closer.

The deal with PSG, who play in the Super Cup final against Aston Villa on Wednesday night in Salzburg, is likely to be worth more than £40m.

Torres only has one year left on his contract at Barcelona and some fans have been frustrated that the forward has spoken openly about the possibility of leaving the club.

Speaking on a media tour of the United States following Spain's World Cup win, he said: "I have a contract with Barcelona but, in football, you never know."

Asked directly about links with PSG, he added: "Every time these teams want you it's a good thing.

"You never know because in football everything can change in one minute, so I have to be ready for everything."

PSG have won the Champions League in the past two seasons and are managed by former Barcelona coach and player Luis Enrique.

The Parisians could lose Bradley Barcola this summer, with the forward wanted by Liverpool.

Torres has been at Barcelona since 2022 having previously spent two years at Manchester City. He has scored 25 goals in 65 appearances for Spain.

title: England gearing up for WXV with new smaller balls
description: England's Red Roses are in pre-season training before the upcoming WXV Global Series and have been using the controversial smaller balls.
fullText:
England's women are in Nottingham for pre-season this month before the upcoming WXV Global Series.

In the new competition, the Red Roses will take on Australia, Canada and New Zealand on home soil in September before further tests across the Atlantic against Canada again and the USA in October.

The last time we saw the world champions in action they were winning another Six Nations' Grand Slam - so what's new?

Head coach John Mitchell spills the beans.

World Rugby's new size 4.5 balls - about 3% smaller but the same weight as a regulation size five - will be used for the WXV Global Series and are now in use in the England camp.

Their introduction has not been without controversy. In May, England fly-half Zoe Harrison said it is "the worst decision someone has ever made".

Mitchell said the attacking players and kickers were all given one to take home for the holidays but he believes "coaching" was key to the success of teams using it.

"If you want to get better at something, regardless of the size of the ball, it's all about coaching. So I think our girls have been well-coached," he said.

"I think it's too early for for me to say that it's going to help our offloading game or it's going to help out with the pass. I'm sure there's consequences as well.

"There might be more contestable kicking, which is probably something that we want to keep away from our game because it's a point of difference between our game and the men's game."

World Rugby held a trial for the smaller balls with female players on the top-tier Sevens circuit in November.

Mitchell said the trial "certainly might help other teams" but he added conclusions would likely be drawn after the first three Tests at home.

During the summer break, Mitchell officially became a UK citizen, external - something he says he should have done "20 years earlier".

Born and raised in New Zealand, the 62-year-old coached the All Blacks to the semi-finals of the 2003 Rugby World Cup but spent much of his early coaching career in England with Sale Sharks, Wasps and as England men's forwards coach.

The citizenship test involves questions about British history and geography as well as singing the national anthem.

Mitchell said his examiner was struggling to find the national anthem music for him so he happily helped her out, explaining: "'I've got it on my Apple Music, is it OK if I play it?' So I played it and I belted it out, and she goes, 'No-one's ever done that before'.

"I said, 'I've had plenty of practice'."

Last month, Gloucester-Hartpury wing Mia Venner and Exeter scrum-half Flo Robinson were awarded full-time England contracts for the first time, among 32 deals for the 2026-27 season.

When asked about Venner and Robinson's contracts, Mitchell said scrum-half Robinson could be an important part of England's plans.

"Will we get Mo [Natasha Hunt] to the next World Cup? We don't know. So it's very important to make sure that we're growing our next player and Flo's definitely taking that on," he said.

Both Gloucester-Hartpury's Hunt, at age 37, and Harlequins' Marlie Packer, 36, are double world champions and included on the Red Roses' latest contract round.

But with Packer admitting she had considered retirement last season, Mitchell explained that for either player to move on, "somebody's got to come and get their jersey" first.

In the off-season it was confirmed Emily Scarratt had joined the Red Roses set-up full-time as attack and backs coach.

Having taken the role on an interim basis during the Six Nations, Mitchell said that the coaching group is "smarter" with Scarratt's inclusion.

However, the new contract appears to come with more responsibility for the former world player of the year.

Mitchell worked with Scarratt on the attack last season but that will start to evolve. He said: "When Em first started, I didn't want to overwhelm her with a with a whole lot of stuff so I gave her a pretty tight remit.

"You just give away a little bit... She certainly has the ability to take the total attack."

The new WXV Global Series doesn't have a table or a trophy attached to it - it is just Test matches.

"There's no tournament to win so we can be very patient about how we go about things," said Mitchell.

Among the six England games are three against Canada. Having beaten them in the 2025 Rugby World Cup final, it is difficult not to see the fixtures as anything other than a three-Test series and Mitchell thinks the prospect is "really cool".

But with England travelling from Manchester to Exeter, to Twickenham, to Canada and the USA, the schedule is a test of its own.

"It's kind of like you're auditioning for Australia 2029 because geographically we're definitely going to be travelling some distance in this tournament," he said.

"So, I think we're trying to mirror that, understand how important our connections are and play exciting rugby."

title: I owe Villa the world but Man Utd are above them - Tielemans
description: Manchester United new boy Youri Tielemans gives his first extended interview on his £35m dream move, making it third time lucky for the ex-Aston Villa man.
fullText:
It was third time lucky this summer in the history of Youri Tielemans and Manchester United.

United looked seriously at the Belgium midfielder in 2019, after Tielemans had impressed in an initial loan spell at Leicester. And again in 2022, as they spent too long holding out for Frenkie de Jong to decide if he was prepared to leave Barcelona.

But it was this July, while the 29-year-old was on World Cup duty, when the Old Trafford outfit made their move, triggering a £35m release clause to snap Tielemans up on a five-year deal from Aston Villa.

"There had been two times that I spoke with the club, but it did not achieve anything," he recalled.

"I was very calm. I was not expecting much this summer, to be fair. I was just focused on my football, focused on the World Cup and trying to perform my best for my country.

"But you know every summer something can happen and obviously I was aware of the clause.

"I am very thankful to Aston Villa. I owe them the world. It is a great club, we did amazing things and they have put me back to my best level. But there are clubs above Villa, and Manchester United is one of them.

"It is a great achievement for any footballer to end up here. It means you have done well in your career. But it does not end there. I want to be successful."

Tielemans cameo against PSG hints at Man Utd future

Man Utd sign Tielemans for £35m from Aston Villa

Tielemans cuts a relaxed figure as he conducts his first extended media interview since his switch from Villa, taking time to personally shake hands with all the journalists present.

He positively beams at points, noticeably when he is asked whether – given he scored Leicester's winner in the 2021 FA Cup final and then the opener for Villa in their Europa League triumph over Freiburg in May – if he can bring goals to Manchester United.

It is also clear from his expression a partnership with skipper Bruno Fernandes is developing.

Senior Manchester United officials noticed it in Gothenburg last weekend, even though the pair were only on the pitch together for 26 minutes in the 1-1 draw with Paris St-Germain.

"It's really natural," he said. "He is a guy that can find space easily. I just try and find him so that he can move forward."

Tielemans is thoughtful though, and expansive in his answers, even if sometimes what he says is not quite what you expect to hear.

One of those is around the length of his career and the number of games he has played.

He made his professional debut for Anderlecht at 16. He has played 668 games for club and country and had to pull out of Belgium's World Cup quarter-final clash with Spain last month after experiencing an issue in the warm-up.

"I feel very good, actually," he said.

"In that last game, it was just an overload of too many games; too many minutes. Unfortunately, my body could not cope with it anymore.

"We played 120 minutes against Senegal, then played the US a few days later, three days after that we played against Spain.

"In the warm-up, my body just switched off for some reason.

"I do not think I am a player that absolutely needs a rest. Obviously, there are a lot of games, and the manager needs to manage the team, but when I am good, I am good.

"When it does not go well, I will know straight away and I will alert the manager. But it does not happen often."

While Tielemans is new to Manchester United, there are some familiar faces helping him to settle in.

Chief among them is Jonny Evans, a former team-mate at Leicester. The pair have remained close and Evans offered a positive character reference to head coach Michael Carrick.

Tielemans also played with Harry Maguire for a short period at Leicester, and Marcus Rashford was a team-mate at Aston Villa.

To the surprise of many, including himself probably, Rashford is back at his boyhood club, having initially left for Villa under a cloud after his fall-out with Ruben Amorim.

"He was great," said Tielemans.

"There had been so much talk about him, bringing pressure and the media around him, but he was so good.

"He was very humble and hard-working, and from the first training session you could tell his touch and acceleration was just amazing. That was what we needed at the time. He did many good things and hopefully he can bring them here."

It could be argued Tielemans' arrival addresses an issue Manchester United has had since Carrick quit in 2018; the scheming midfielder with an eye for a pass, who can break a defensive line.

In theory, it will allow Fernandes more room further forward and offer the opportunity to control games for a team that has, in recent times, tended to be viewed as being better on the counter-attack.

Tielemans had a brief chat with Carrick before he completed his move.

But the past 10 days have offered a great insight into Carrick's expectations.

"He wants me to be free on the pitch, to try and organise the team the best I can," he said.

"He has got his structure. He wants to have the ball and wants to press in certain ways.

"It might be different than what I am used to, but it is logical things in my opinion.

"It is just smelling football, which is what I have been doing from when I was young at Anderlecht, you know.

"For me, nothing changes, but it just needs to gel together."

title: Why is the women's 800m record so tough to break?
description: The world record for the women's 800m is the longest-standing in athletics. No-one has managed to break it for 43 years. Why?
fullText:
The world record for the women's 800m is the longest-standing in athletics. No-one has managed to break it for 43 years.

So why, despite leaps forward in shoe technology and our understanding of nutrition and recovery, has that record not fallen?

Great Britain's Keely Hodgkinson is one of the top three middle-distance runners in the world competing at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham this week. So could that record, finally, be broken?

The women's 800m world record is held by Czech athlete Jarmila Kratochvilova, who ran a time of one minute 53.28 seconds in 1983.

There have been claims that Kratochvilova's performance in Munich was assisted by the systematic doping regime that existed in her country at the time - something she has strenuously denied.

Kratochvilova's record is not the only one to be questioned.

Marita Koch of East Germany set the women's 400m record two years later, in 1985 - when the country was known to be systematically doping its athletes.

But Koch never failed a drugs test, and always maintained she did nothing wrong.

In 2017, European Athletics proposed wiping out records set before 2005.

The proposals never went any further. But they sent a strong signal that some records set before 2005 - when World Athletics (formerly IAAF) started storing blood and urine samples - could be disputed.

Back in 1983, then 32-year-old Kratochvilova crossed the finish line more than seven seconds ahead of her closest rival, Poland's Jolanta Januchta.

No-one would come within a second of Kratochvilova's record for 25 years.

The closest any athlete has come to breaking it is Swiss athlete Audrey Werro, who ran a time of 1:53.80 in June this year.

Hodgkinson and gold medal rivals progress at Europeans

"Believe you me, that time of 1:53.28 is astonishing," Jenny Meadows, former British runner and coach to Hodgkinson, told BBC Sport.

"I won medals on a global level and I could not even comprehend that a female could run that sort of time."

But athletes have never been closer to breaking it.

Werro has twice gone under 1:54 this year, but still more than half a second from Kratochvilova's record.

Olympic champion Hodgkinson broke the 800m indoor record in February, which had stood since 2002, crossing the line in 1:54.87.

Then there's the Netherlands' Femke Broeders-Bol, still largely an unknown in the 800m after deciding to switch disciplines from 400m hurdles. But, with little 800m experience, she ran a time of 1:55.60 seconds at the Paris Diamond League event in June.

"They're all dragging each other to these incredible times. The level of the 800m has risen significantly in the past two years," said Jessica Ennis-Hill, who won heptathlon gold at the London 2012 Olympics.

Innovations in sports science have edged athletes closer too.

"Everyone is going faster than they used to be because the shoe technology is so much better," University of Exeter professor Andrew Jones told BBC Sport.

Jones specialises in applied physiology, working with middle and long-distance runners to chase faster times.

"We know more about various supplements, things like creatine, nitrate, but in particular bicarbonate.

"And we know more about what limits performance".

This includes our understanding of carbohydrates, and how to best fuel for a middle-distance race like the 800m.

"It's a bit like a Formula One race car," he added. "You want the car to cross the line almost empty of fuel. If you've got half a tank left, you've been weighing yourself down."

Now, in Birmingham, the best three 800m runners in the world are looking like they will contest a gripping final, if they come through Thursday's semi-finals. Whether that final will turn into a more tactical race or develop into a battle of speed remains to be seen.

"All it takes is one person to raise the bar and you think more things are possible," Hodgkinson told BBC Sport.

"Everyone knows that to keep up you have to keep getting better. It's a really exciting time for the women's 800m."

title: Zhang shocks Zhao in final-ball respot at China Open
description: Zhang Anda shocked world number three Zhao Xintong with a thrilling 6-5 victory by potting a respotted black ball in round one of the China Open.
fullText:
Zhang Anda shocked world number three Zhao Xintong with a thrilling 6-5 victory by potting a respotted black ball in round one of the China Open.

Zhang, who was down 3-0 in frames, fought back to eventually lead 5-4.

However, last year's world champion Zhao forced a deciding frame that ended in dramatic fashion.

"Today was just my day," Zhang said. "I hope that I can go far [in this tournament], I don't want them [two pots of the black] again. I was too nervous."

Zhang, ranked 19th in the world, was in control at 57-0 up, but Zhao fought back to lead with both players on the black.

The black was eventually potted by Zhang to force a respot - used as a tie-breaker when a frame ends with the scores level - with the 34-year-old prevailing.

He will now face England's Chris Wakelin.

"I made far too many mistakes today and I probably didn't deserve to win," Zhao added.

"I had prepared well for coming to Shanxi this time, and I didn't expect to lose in the first round. I played too badly and there was nothing I could do about it."

World number five John Higgins also lost in the first round after he was defeated 6-4 by 2015 world champion Stuart Bingham.

title: Doku 'not against' journalist who criticised him at World Cup

fullText:
Jeremy Doku says he is "not against" the journalist who criticised his plan to leave the Belgium camp during the World Cup to attend the birth of his first child.

Doku's wife Shireen was due to give birth during the second week of July and he told Reuters, external before the start of the tournament he intended to leave the camp to be at the birth even if his side were still in contention.

But it brought fierce criticism from L'Equipe channel presenter France Pierron, who labelled a father "completely useless" at the time of their child's birth.

L'Equipe later apologised and said Pierron's comments were "very far removed" from its values. The presenter also apologised but was taken off air until the end of the season of her show.

Doku eventually missed Belgium's 0-0 draw against Iran in the group stage to fly back to the UK for the birth of his son, Praise.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, external, Doku said he understood why some people questioned the timing of events.

"There was a lot of noise of course," the Manchester City winger said.

"I can understand why people felt like maybe this was orchestrated because it was too perfect.

"I also saw the journalist speak about me and the situation and all the people getting at her. But I just wanted to use this video as well to really... pray over her.

"I don't want to come at her in a way that most people did. I don't want people to be too harsh on her. We don't know what she has experienced. It's her opinion.

"She got fired and all these things. I never want this for a person. I'm not against her. I'm not angry at her or anything. She just said her opinion."

Doku played 86 minutes of Belgium's opening 1-1 draw with Egypt in Group G of the World Cup before missing their next game, with his absence explained as illness.

A Belgium statement later said, external that the 24-year-old travelled to London to be with his wife "with the approval of and accompanied by one of our team doctors".

title: Duan Jansen, Marco’s twin brother, earns maiden South Africa call-up for Namibia tour
description: Duan Jansen, twin brother of Marco, has received his maiden South Africa call-up for the Namibia tour. Bjorn Fortuin will captain the squad, while several domestic performers have earned opportunities to strengthen South Africa’s international depth.
fullText:
Duan Jansen, twin brother of South Africa all-rounder Marco Jansen, has earned his maiden senior call-up and could make his international debut during South Africa's upcoming white-ball tour of Namibia.

The 15-member squad, led by experienced spinner Bjorn Fortuin, will play a T20I tri-series involving Namibia and Zimbabwe before taking on Namibia in a historic three-match ODI series.

The T20I tri-series will be played in Windhoek from August 28 to September 6, followed by three ODIs against Namibia from September 9 to 13. The ODI series will be the first bilateral 50-over contest between the two neighbouring countries.

Duan's selection comes after an impressive 2025/26 domestic season. He was named Division 1 One Day Cup Player of the Year and played a key role in helping the Titans win the title, scoring an unbeaten 61 in the final against the Lions.

Eathan Bosch is the other uncapped T20I player, while Connor Esterhuizen, Jordan Hermann and Nqobani Mokoena have received their first ODI call-ups.

"We've selected one squad for both series as we feel we have all departments well covered and it provides a great opportunity for players to build on their international caps. We saw glimpses of what Connor and Nqobani can offer during the T20I series against New Zealand earlier this year. It was unfortunate that Jordan picked up an injury in the opening match of that series, so we're looking forward to seeing him get another opportunity at this level."

Coach Shukri Conrad said using the same squad for both formats would give the players greater continuity and valuable international exposure. Nationally contracted players Dewald Brevis, Tony de Zorzi and Kwena Maphaka will provide additional experience.

"This tour has also opened the door for players who have performed domestically. Duan is one of those players. He is a quality all-rounder who has also shown great character for the Titans. Bjorn is an experienced player and proven leader who has successfully captained the Lions, and we have every confidence in his ability to lead this group. It is always exciting to play against our neighbouring countries, and the first-ever ODI series between South Africa and Namibia adds further significance, especially as we build towards next year's World Cup," he added.

South Africa are scheduled to leave Johannesburg for Windhoek on August 25.

title: Women's football shouldn't be penalised by Uefa boycott - Nandy
description: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy says women's footballers should not be "penalised" by a potential boycott of next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup.
fullText:
Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy says women's footballers should not be "penalised" by a potential boycott of next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup, as hosts Poland say they have received no notice of any withdrawals from European teams.

European governing body Uefa and its 55 members have threatened to boycott Fifa competitions over its president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup.

Poland are due to host the tournament from 5-27 September, but are not the only Uefa nation involved - with England, Italy, Spain, Portugal and France all due to take part.

The Polish Football Association (PZPN) told BBC Sport on Tuesday that it had so far "not received any information regarding the possible withdrawal of any participating team from the tournament".

It added: "We believe that the current situation will be resolved swiftly, allowing young players from across the world to compete in Poland.

"Our priority remains to ensure the best possible conditions for the competition and for all participating teams. For many of these young players, this tournament represents an important milestone in their sporting careers, and we remain fully focused on delivering an event worthy of their talent and commitment."

Last week, the French Football Federation (FFF) said it intended to compete at the U20 World Cup while the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) also told BBC Sport that "so far, the Under-20 team is complying with the planned programme", including a friendly fixture against England later this week.

England's Football Association has not confirmed whether it will field a team for the World Cup. However, as things stand, coach Lydia Bedford's Young Lionesses squad are continuing preparations for the tournament.

The map showing world's division over Infantino

Trump says it would be 'terrible mistake' to remove Infantino

Nandy told the BBC that she wants to see Infantino resign over his Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, under which stakes in the World Cup and other competitions would be sold to private investors.

"We support the [English] FA in saying that football belongs to its fans, enough is enough, and it is time for a change at Fifa," Nandy said.

"I think [Infantino] should go, the time is up."

But she added she would not support a boycott of the U20 World Cup.

"I am not generally in favour of sporting boycotts full stop, because I think they divide people from one another, I think they unfairly penalise athletes and competitors who are not responsible for the reason that these boycotts take place," she said.

"What I would like to see actually is football coming together, resolving this, a change of leadership, a change of direction and a very clear message that football belongs to its fans and it will not have women and girls penalised when the women's game is going from strength to strength. And our Lionesses are leading the world in that."

fullText:
Music streaming platform creates ‘AI persona’ label that will appear on profiles and track listings in crackdown on fake performers

Spotify is to label AI artists and exclude them from algorithm recommendations as part of a crackdown on fake performers.

The world’s largest music streaming platform is creating a label for AI-generated artist identities called “AI personas” that will appear on the artist profile and on track listings on playlists.

It means that from September AI-generated artists such as the Velvet Sundown will carry the persona label and will be blocked from personalised recommendations by default. The aim is to differentiate these deepfake artists from real performers who might lose out on streams to artificial rivals.

Spotify said: “True artist-fan connection can only be built on a foundation of trust and authenticity. In music, that means listeners need to be able to trust that the artist behind the music is who they say they are. That’s more essential than ever in the age of generative AI.”

Last year Spotify revealed it had removed 75m spam tracks from its platform over a 12-month period as AI tools created a flood of fake music. Spotify’s legitimate catalogue stands at 100m tracks.

Spotify will allow music creators to reveal if their identities are AI-created – and will then label them as an AI persona – but it will not rely on self-disclosure alone. The company said it would use human review and AI investigative tools to determine if artists were fake. Although the new rule technically applies to AI “identities”, Spotify says AI-generated profiles are invariably a front for AI-made tracks as well.

The company said: “Listeners have been clear in telling us that they don’t like seeing an artist profile that seems human, only to find out that the persona is AI-generated.”

Last year there was debate about the origins of the Velvet Sundown – a 70s-style US rock band – before the band’s social media channels confirmed the subterfuge. A statement described the group as an AI creation that was “somewhere in between” human and machine.

The Velvet Sundown has 117,000 monthly listeners on Spotify but its page has no clear AI labelling, although the artist profile describes the four-piece as a “synthetic music project”.

In January there was further discussion about Sienna Rose, a soul singer who entered Spotify’s viral top 50 but did not appear to be real, having never played a gig or released any videos despite releasing a prolific burst of material over a 10-week period. The Spotify profile for Rose, who has more than half a million monthly listeners, does not clarify whether she is AI or not.

fullText:
North Texas has beaten some of the world's biggest data center hubs to claim the No. 1 spot in a new global ranking, as Texas becomes an increasingly powerful player in the industry.

Dallas ranked No. 1 in the 2026 Global Data Center Market Comparison by Cushman & Wakefield, a global commercial real estate services firm. The Lone Star State made a strong showing across the board, with Austin-San Antonio and West Texas also ranking first in their respective categories.

The rankings underscore how quickly Texas has become a major destination for data center development as companies search for the land and electricity needed to support artificial intelligence and other computing. Cushman & Wakefield said the state is growing at a pace that could eventually match, or surpass, Virginia, the world's largest data center market by operating capacity.

Dallas isn't the world's largest data center market. Despite Dallas' No. 1 ranking, Virginia remains the world's largest data center market based on the amount of capacity already in operation.

Cushman & Wakefield's ranking, however, looks beyond sheer size to where the industry is positioned to grow. The commercial real estate services firm compared 107 markets on factors including access to power and land, projects under construction, existing infrastructure and the regulatory environment.

Dallas has one of the largest pipelines of planned data center development, trailing only Virginia and Atlanta, according to the report. And that development is spreading across Texas.

Cushman & Wakefield said activity has pushed outward from the long-established Dallas-Fort Worth market as companies search for vast amounts of land and electricity needed to support AI and other computing. At the current pace, the firm said Texas could eventually match or surpass Virginia in total data center capacity.

Texas has several advantages in that race, including abundant land, a business-friendly environment, an independent and deregulated power grid and incentives for development, according to the report.

The rapid growth has also drawn political attention, with Texas Gov. Greg Abbott pressing data centers to provide more of their own power and cover infrastructure costs as development accelerates across the state.

title: Are Man Utd judged differently to other WSL sides?
description: Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, but is the women's team really judged differently as a result?
fullText:
Manchester United's women's side were in the headlines again last week for the wrong reasons following the departure of former manager Marc Skinner.

The club have been heavily criticised for their apparent lack of investment in the women's team since it was reformed as a professional outfit in 2018.

Quiet transfer windows, high-profile departures, a lack of silverware and scrutiny over facilities have been well documented.

Sources at the club have voiced frustrations over their treatment in the media and it escalated last season when The Athletic were banned, external from asking questions in a post-match huddle with Skinner.

Manchester United are proud to call themselves one of the biggest clubs in the world, but are they judged differently as a result?

Have Man Utd lost faith in their women's team?

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Skinner's departure came after months of hints at his frustrations over the lack of investment in his squad.

His side finished inside the Women's Super League's top three on two occasions, reached three successive FA Cup finals, delivered a first major trophy and made it to the quarter-finals of the Champions League at the first time of asking.

Some criticism towards Skinner came from United's own fanbase, as they held banners up at Leigh Sports Village calling for his sacking in 2024.

Unhappiness also appeared to be based on their performances against their WSL top-three rivals Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester City, rather than just results.

Meanwhile, media repeatedly pointed out the club's lack of investment, which followed ex-manager Casey Stoney stepping down in 2021 because of growing concerns over a lack of resources and the state of facilities.

United took so long to form a professional women's set-up that when they did in 2018 - hiring Stoney as manager and recruiting a number of Lionesses, including current Manchester City captain Alex Greenwood to play in the second tier - the assumption was they intended to battle it out with England's elite.

But eight years on, they have delivered just one major trophy and are in danger of slipping below their rivals again this season.

High-profile reports on United's inadequate training facilities circled in 2024 when the women's team were moved out of their Carrington training site and into temporary buildings to make way for the men's first team.

Co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe's comments about the women's team were also scrutinised. Speaking to the United We Stand fanzine, Ratcliffe described the men's team as the "main issue" and referred to the women's side as "girls" and "an opportunity".

United also lost a number of key first-team members of staff.

Former assistant coach Martin Ho is now enjoying success as Tottenham manager and was joined by goalkeeping coach Ian Willcock in April, while another former assistant, Charlotte Healy, became head coach at WSL 2 club Bristol City last year.

Big-name players, including England duo Alessia Russo and Mary Earps, as well as Spain full-back Ona Batlle, were allowed to leave on free transfers.

This summer, they lost their star striker Melvine Malard to rivals Chelsea and are yet to sign a replacement, although the £850,000 fee will prove useful.

Given the talent at United's disposal during their eight-year existence, it is understandable that questions have been asked over the club's inability to keep hold of them.

United's reputation, built on the history of the men's teams' successes, means fans demand trophies and expect to see ambition.

That is no different to other big clubs, such as Liverpool, West Ham or Tottenham, who all have women's teams that have been competing at a lower level.

Spurs did not gain promotion to the WSL until 2019 and have been flirting with lower and mid-table spots until more recently under Ho.

West Ham remain the only WSL team not to have played at their men's stadium and have consistently been criticised for not investing in the transfer window.

Former West Ham head coach Rehanne Skinner had to make structural changes and ex vice-chair Karren Brady was not seen at WSL games and they frequently lost key players.

Liverpool, in particular, have faced huge scrutiny over the treatment of their women's team - who were back-to-back WSL title winners in 2013 and 2014 but were relegated in 2020.

They also faced scathing criticism about their pitch conditions in 2019.

In 2021, former Liverpool players Kirsty Linnett and Becky Jane took to social media to claim contracts they were offered were retracted by the club.

Even Chelsea, who won six successive WSL titles, were criticised for capping the number of spectators they allowed into Stamford Bridge for Women's Champions League games in order to reduce costs of running the stadium on matchdays.

Their manager Sonia Bompastor called for better recruitment and more squad depth last season.

In summary, Manchester United have faced significant scrutiny, but they are one of many WSL clubs whose decisions and progress have been closely examined.

title: The map showing world's division over Infantino
description: BBC Sport uses visuals to explore the support and opposition to Gianni Infantino's leadership of Fifa from its members.
fullText:
As recently as mid-July, Gianni Infantino was considered a shoo-in to be re-elected as Fifa president next March.

All but a handful of Fifa's 210 members had endorsed his bid for a fourth term in charge of world football, and he faced no meaningful challenge from any quarter.

But that picture looks very different now, after two weeks of relentless fallout to his now-abandoned plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors.

The world is far from united over whether Infantino should stay or go.

To illustrate that division, BBC Sport has mapped the apparent view of all 210 member associations who are able to vote (Nepal, Fifa's 211th member, is currently suspended and has no voting rights).

In some cases, countries have publicly stated their overt support or opposition regarding Infantino.

Others have directly told BBC Sport where they stand when asked to do so, while some are assumed positions based on statements made by the continental confederation the country sits within.

Trump says it would be 'terrible mistake' to remove Infantino

Whereas once Infantino looked set to saunter to a fourth term unopposed, he now might need to have enough numbers on his side to stay in post.

If a unity candidate is found to oppose him, then the election would become a direct battle.

Fifa election votes between two candidates require a simple majority - each candidate would require a total of 106 votes to win.

If there are three or more candidates, a first-round win requires two thirds of the vote. If there is no winner, there is a second round where a simple majority is needed.

Europe has 55 votes, Africa 54, Asia 46, North America 35, Oceania 11 and South America 10.

But while the current tally looks like 73 in support of Infantino, 124 in opposition to him and 13 undecided, that picture is fluid and is likely to change in the months ahead.

Several European countries, including England and Wales, have formally withdrawn letters of support for Infantino that they had sent for next year's election.

On Monday, the backlash against Infantino intensified when European governing body Uefa, North America's Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) signed a joint letter accusing him and Fifa of breaking their trust "through deception".

It is a significant coalition, and those regional governing bodies represent 136 associations between them.

But there are already dissenting members within the confederations, like Bhutan, the Philippines, and the UAE within Asia, who have all backed Infantino.

Indeed, Asia is considered a potential swing region for Infantino's future, with many associations not yet making their position known.

Mexico has broken ranks within Concacaf by coming out in support of Infantino, too. The USA and Canada have stated support for Concacaf's latest statement, but have not outright declared their opposition to Infantino's rule.

And the Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) has made no public comment since the whole saga began - nor have any of its members. OFC told BBC Sport they will release a statement following a meeting on Thursday.

Infantino still has staunch allies too, particularly within Africa (Caf) and South America (Conmebol), who have benefited from unprecedented investment since he took over a decade ago.

That investment could help him gain critical votes from nations within AFC, Concacaf and OFC - who are lower down the football food chain and have benefited significantly from the Fifa Forward programme, which has made billions of dollars available for investment.

And Saudi Arabia - which has yet to take a public position but was awarded hosting rights for the 2034 World Cup on Infantino's watch - will have its own football leadership elections in August. The results could dictate the kingdom's position, and influence the view of others in the region.

It cannot be guaranteed that every nation will toe the line of their confederation.

Infantino has shown no desire to step down, but there is a chance that his time in charge could be over by the autumn.

That could come to pass if Fifa Council members try to force his resignation at an emergency meeting.

Such a meeting can be called, and must take place within a fortnight, if 19 of the 37 members call for it.

The council is made up of nine members from Uefa, seven from AFC, six from Caf, five from Concacaf, five from Conmebol, and three from Oceania. Also on the panel are Infantino himself and Fifa secretary general Mattias Grafstrom.

Given its makeup, then, this approach is probably unlikely.

Which leaves the possibility of a candidate standing against Infantino next March. Nobody has put their name forward yet, but if the leaders of Uefa, Concacaf, and AFC are serious about toppling Infantino, uniting behind a single candidate is likely their best option.

The deadline for a candidate to announce their intention to stand is November.

Historically, other confederations have been angered by European dominance of football, its competitions and its wealth.

That is perhaps why Concacaf president Victor Montagliani has been consistently mooted as the most likely challenger to Infantino in recent weeks.

The map of votes could change significantly based on who stands.

If AFC president Sheikh Salman were to step forward, for example, there is a chance that could sway some of the associations in Asia that are currently supportive of Infantino towards him.

For now, the global picture remains unclear because of emerging splits within confederations, the potential for key players to declare one way or another in the coming months and the hitherto lack of a clear candidate to challenge Infantino.

What is clear is that Infantino is no longer coasting towards a fourth term, if he clings on that long.

title: Trump says would be 'terrible mistake' to oust embattled Infantino
description: US President Donald Trump said on Monday it would be "a terrible mistake" to replace Gianni Infantino, the embattled FIFA president who tried, and failed, to sell off part of the World Cup to private investors."FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino," Trump posted on Truth Social.
fullText:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday it would be "a terrible mistake" to replace Gianni Infantino, the embattled FIFA president who tried, and failed, to sell off part of the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino came under renewed fire in an open letter signed by three confederations -- Europe's UEFA, North and Central America's CONCACAF and Asia's AFC -- accusing the world football boss of breaking trust "through deception".

But Trump backed Infantino, who awarded the US president a "FIFA Peace Prize" at the World Cup draw ceremony last year.

"FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino," Trump posted on Truth Social.

Trump called Infantino "fantastic" and said he "presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented".

"If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!" added Trump, who attended the World Cup final with Infantino last month.

Trump's backing of Infantino is at odds with US Soccer, who joined the voices lining up against the FIFA president.

Infantino launched, and then withdrew in the face of scathing criticism, a plan to bring private investment into FIFA competitions, including World Cups.

FIFA hit back on Saturday at efforts "to undermine" football's governing body and Infantino.

However, Monday's joint letter from UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC retorted: "Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding -- or demanding -- power to be held.

"When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned."

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is viewed as a potential challenger to Infantino, who will be up for re-election for a fourth and final term at the FIFA Congress in March, 2027. Candidates have to be declared by November 18.

Infantino had looked certain to be unopposed for a fourth term after overseeing a successful World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada until his plans were revealed.

The 56-year-old Swiss, who has been in situ for 10 years, has received the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) while South American governing body CONMEBOL is largely supportive.

Individual member associations, not confederations, vote in the FIFA election,

Infantino has received support from CONCACAF's Mexico and two AFC members -- Kuwait and 2022 World Cup hosts Qatar, where he has a house.

UEFA's threat to boycott World Cups if the private investment plan went ahead proved pivotal in Infantino withdrawing his sell-off plan.

UEFA had called it "a shabby, opaque, backroom deal" and lashed out at Infantino again on Monday for a "failure of judgment".

After the furore, Infantino received "full support" of senior FIFA directors in an emergency meeting in Morocco last week, but the three confederations said that was meaningless.

The recent meeting, where "a select number of members of the FIFA Management Committee" were present, they said, "represents a continuation of the very pattern of conduct that brought us to this moment".

"It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him."

Infantino had been basking in the afterglow of the largest ever World Cup involving 48 teams until his plans divided the sport.

"The growth over the past decade has been real. But that progress was never the work of one individual," declared the letter.

"It was the product of FIFA, the Confederations, the Member Associations, and the thousands of people who dedicate their lives to the game.

"The expanded tournaments... were shared achievements, agreed together, delivered together."

Under Infantino's leadership "there is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness", they said.

"That is why we have taken this stance: not lightly and not alone, but together, and out of duty to the game we serve.

"Football's strength has always been its unity."

fullText:
Men's tennis is in the dog days of summer, and it's missing its two biggest stars.

Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner have both pulled out of the Canadian and Cincinnati opens – the two biggest lead-up tournaments to the US Open.

For Sinner, the World No. 1 hasn't played a tournament since lifting the trophy at Wimbledon on July 12. It's been an even longer wait for Carlos Alcaraz. The Spaniard and Australian Open champion has been sidelined with a wrist injury since April, missing both the French Open and Wimbledon.

We've seen plenty of tournaments to feature Sinner without Alcaraz. It isn't the same. The cool, mechanic Sinner is not compelling to watch without his freewheeling rival who prefers to hit the flair shot rather than the highest percentage possible (oftentimes to the crowd's delight). The tennis world needs its sun and moon.

Now, the two biggest men's stars on the planet are injured when the tennis calendar is supposed to be reaching its crescendo.

Instead, the men's tour is left with a wide-open field and substandard competition. The final eight of the Canadian Open consist of only one player inside the top eight: Ben Shelton. Alex Zverev lost in the early stages.

There has been some discourse about the length of these tournaments. Both Canada and Cincinnati are two-week events – which is quite a long time for a non-major (if you aren't Indian Wells or Miami). And to hold them in the tail end of the season is especially difficult. Novak Djokovic is also skipping them.

It makes for few compelling matches. Perhaps the only one that was interesting was Shelton taking on Brazilian upstard Joao Fonseca in the fourth round.

Otherwise, we're watching the meteoric rise of Rafael Jodar. The 19-year-old player from Madrid is in his first year as a pro, and he's making serious waves. He's already breached top 15 and through to the quarterfinals in Canada.

In a world where we're craving someone to challenge Sinner and Alcaraz, Jodar could be the guy. I've previously written it could be Fonseca too. It's still early days. The only thing that's for sure is we can't make any definitive statements until Sinner and Alcaraz return to the court.

title: Aryna Sabalenka’s ‘Tough Spot’ Involving Elena Rybakina Draws Steve Johnson’s Verdict After Toronto Exit

fullText:
Aryna Sabalenka has not made the best start to her North American hardcourt swing, crashing out of the Canadian Open in the fourth round. Former American player Steve Johnson has shared his insight into what could be affecting the world No. 1's performance on the court.

Following her fourth-round exit at Wimbledon, Sabalenka enjoyed a brief break before arriving at the WTA 1000 event in Toronto. She looked refreshed and in good touch as she kicked off her campaign by defeating Moyuka Uchijima and Zhang Shuai in straight sets.

However, Ekaterina Alexandrova presented a far tougher challenge in their fourth-round encounter. Although Sabalenka fought back strongly after losing the first set and even saved two match points in the decider, Alexandrova eventually claimed a 7-6 (3), 4-6, 6-4 victory.

Speaking on the "Nothing Major" podcast, Steve Johnson highlighted the world No. 1's impressive 24-1 winning record on hard courts in the first half of the 2026 season. He suggested that Sabalenka was expected to maintain that same level of dominance on the surface after relatively underwhelming results on clay and grass.

"Sabalanka, after Wimbledon, she was like, 'I'm going away from tennis.' She wants to go on vacation, get drunk, and kind of reset. And that was important for her because she was 24-1 on hard courts this year leading up to this, from obviously start of the year through Miami, she won the Sunshine double, final in Australia, won Brisbane," Johnson said.

"So, she has been absolutely dominant on the hardcourts and you felt like she was going to get back to that, but she played pretty good in her first match and then, you know, she ends up losing to Ekaterina Alexandrova in a tough three setter," he added.

However, Johnson feels that Sabalenka is in a "tough spot" as she attempts to rediscover her best level while dealing with the threat of Elena Rybakina, who is closing in on the world No. 1 ranking.

"I thought she did a good job battling back, but it just feels like she's anxious out there, right? She wants to win. She wants to get back to where she was. And that's a tough spot to be in because I feel like for Sabalenka, with how much kind of personality and fun she can have on the court, when she's having fun, I feel like she plays better," he said.

Rybakina, who is through to the quarterfinals in Toronto, would pull to within just four points of Sabalenka's top spot (8,670 to 8,666) if she clinches the Canadian Open title.

"And it just feels like right now she's gripping the racket a little tight. She could lose her No. 1 spot in the world coming up if Rybakina has a good week here in Montreal and in Cincinnati," Johnson added.

title: Mark Zuckerberg says the future will have an ‘abundance of jobs’—and predicts a wave of new careers like world builders and personal biologists
description: Despite predictions of a job apocalypse, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg sees a future of economic and financial prosperity.
fullText:
The rise of superintelligence—technology capable of surpassing human cognitive abilities—has fueled fears ranging from an elimination of human labor to more dystopian, Terminator-like visions of what happens when technology goes rogue. But now, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is pushing back against the predictions of a job apocalypse once made by his fellow tech CEOs, including Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman.

"I do not understand why anyone who believes that AI will eliminate most jobs and much of humanity's relevance would rush to build that future," Zuckerberg wrote in an essay posted to Meta's website Monday.

"The notion that AI is so dangerous that the only safe path is an extreme concentration of power seems inherently problematic. Historically, hoping that an absolute power will benevolently provide for humanity if sufficiently enlightened has not led to safe or positive outcomes."

Zuckerberg, who is the world's sixth-richest person with a net worth of $211 billion, sees AI as a catalyst for an "abundance of jobs in the future," arguing that people will continue to invent new products and services—and the jobs needed to bring them to life.

He pointed to the fact that a generation ago, commonplace jobs like app developers, social media creators, electric vehicle technicians, and data center operators barely existed.

And moving forward, the 42-year-old expects a new set of careers to come into being, such as one-person-studio designers creating physical products, world builders devising virtual experiences, and personal biologists formulating individualized treatments.

Despite Zuckerberg's largely optimistic tone, he acknowledged that the transition could still come with growing pains. If automation outpaces workers' ability to develop new skills, job displacement could create a "difficult period" for society.

That disruption could be particularly painful without greater investment in training workers in career paths less vulnerable to automation, such as in the skilled trades.

"Unlike the concern about knowledge work displacement, there is a shortage of skilled tradespeople like carpenters, electricians, and construction workers to support the demand for infrastructure buildout," he said.

Earlier this year, Meta committed $115 million into building out America's Workforce Academy—a training program designed to prepare workers for data center technician roles. The five-week program provides training at no cost, and graduates are guaranteed a job at one of Meta's data center sites.

title: Russian Athletics files new claim against sanctions
description: The Russian Athletics Ferderation files a new claim with the Court of Arbitration for Sport to challenge the sanctions imposed by World Athletics.
fullText:
The Russian Athletics Federation has filed a new claim with the Court of Arbitration for Sport to challenge sanctions imposed by World Athletics.

Athletes from Russia and Belarus have been banned from international competition under the world governing body since the country's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Russian Athletics says the ongoing sanctions "infringe on the organisation's rights", adding they "prevent it from fully representing the interests of Russian athletes on an international level."

The International Olympic Committee provisionally lifted Russia's suspension in July, potentially allowing the country to compete at the 2028 Olympics Games in Los Angeles.

Cas, based in Lausanne, Switzerland, serves as sport's highest arbitration body and hears disputes involving athletes, federations and governing organisations.

"The sanctions against Russian Athletics are unprecedented. No other sports federation faces such severe restrictions," Boris Yaryshevskiy, chief executive director of Russian Athletics, said in a statement.

"They not only hinder the federation's normal operation but also hold back the development of athletics in Russia, particularly among young athletes, preventing us from properly representing our sport in the international arena.

"That is why we will consistently defend our rights, pursue the lifting of the sanctions through the courts, and continue our work in this direction. We are already preparing our next steps to restore justice."

Russian Athletics lodged a separate appeal on 9 July challenging a decision by the World Athletics Council - the main rule-making and executive body of World Athletics - to extend the ban on Russian athletes from international events.

Other sporting federations, including World Gymnastics, World Aquatics and World Boxing, have this year eased restrictions on Russian athletes competing.

Some Russian and Belarusian athletes competed as neutrals at both the 2024 Paris Games and this year's Winter Olympics in Milan.

title: Parkinson withdraws from England Under-20 camp

fullText:
Teenager Erica Meg Parkinson has withdrawn from England's training camp before the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Poland next month.

The North Carolina Courage midfielder, 18, was named in Lydia Bedford's 24-player squad for the warm-weather camp in Portugal, but has decided to stay with her club instead.
